title: Stellar LLC — cost delta analysis after Redwood Optimize recommendations
content:
Executive summary:

This sheet captures a granular before/after cost comparison for Stellar LLC (public web search assistant) assuming we implement the Redwood Optimize recommendations completed during the week of 2024-10-07. The model mix before Optimize was: base-7b-fp16 for short queries and base-13b-fp16 for long queries. After recommendations we propose: unified base-13b-int8 + aggressive KV/prefix caching + request-level batching (dynamic window) + routing to spot-dedicated pool for non-SLA traffic.

Key findings (headline numbers):
- Baseline monthly inference spend (current pipeline): $142,300
- Projected monthly spend after Optimize (recommended config): $67,850
- Estimated monthly savings: $74,450 (52.4% reduction)
- Time to implement (engineering + rollout): 4–6 weeks with staged canary

Methodology & assumptions (important):
- Workload: 3.2M requests/day (avg), 1.8 tokens/request avg, 95th percentile length mix: 70% short (<32 tokens), 30% long (avg 512 tokens).
- Traffic shape: 63% daytime skew; 20% peak-minute concentration.
- Baseline serving config: mixture of on-demand hosted vCPU+GPU endpoints using fp16 weights; no prefix caching; naive per-request scheduling (no batching).
- Unit costs used (baseline): $0.022 per GPU-minute for 7b-fp16, $0.035 per GPU-minute for 13b-fp16 (apportioned to per-token cost based on throughput profiles). Infra overhead (network, storage, control) added 12% to token-level cost.
- Post-optimize assumptions: INT8 quantization reduces per-token GPU compute by 45% vs fp16 for 13b; batching (avg effective batch size 12 during non-peak, 6 during peak) reduces per-token overhead by additional 18%; KV/prefix cache hit rate conservatively 27% (saves full forward pass tokens on hits); routing of 40% of background traffic to reserved spot pool at 30% lower infra price.
- Quality guardrails: we recommend AB test emitted quality on a 5% sample before full switch. Quantized outputs validated on 5000 eval prompts (delta BLEU-like / embedding distance within acceptable threshold).

Detailed numbers (spreadsheet export style):

Rows: Category | Baseline monthly $ | After-optimize monthly $ | Delta $ | Delta %
1. Model compute (token-level) | $105,400 | $47,300 | -$58,100 | -55.1%
2. Infra overhead (network/control) | $16,200 | $7,600 | -$8,600 | -53.1%
3. Storage & logs | $5,700 | $5,200 | -$500 | -8.8%
4. Observability + tracing ingestion | $3,000 | $3,000 | $0 | 0%
5. Reserved capacity amortization (dedicated/spot) | $11,000 | $4,750 | -$6,250 | -56.8%
TOTAL | $142,300 | $67,850 | -$74,450 | -52.4%

Breakdown commentary: Model compute sees the largest impact from quantization + batching + caching. The storage/logging line is mostly unaffected because we keep 30-day retention; recommend reducing to 14-day for further savings (see sensitivity below). Observability costs are fixed for now due to SLAs. Reserved capacity drops because we shift cold/background load to spot-reserved pools and consolidate model variants.

Per-token math (simplified):
- Baseline per-request token cost: (short avg 1.2 tokens/request): 1.2 * baseline-token-rate = $0.000013 per request short; long requests average 512 tokens => baseline per-request token cost $0.0067; blended across traffic -> baseline token spend ~ $3.3M tokens/day leading to $105.4k/month compute.
- After Optimize per-token compute reductions: quantization 45% + batching 18% (applied multiplicatively) -> ~61% compute reduction on non-cache tokens. Cache hits (27%) avoid full forward pass; we approximate they save 100% of long token compute and 60% of short token compute (prefix reuse partial).

Sensitivity analysis (three scenarios):
- Conservative: cache hit rate 15%, batching avg size 6 -> projected savings 34% ($48k/month).
- Base (our projection used above): cache 27%, batching avg 9 -> 52% savings ($74k/month).
- Aggressive: cache 40%, batching avg 14, more routing to spot -> 67% savings ($95k/month).

Implementation plan (phases):
- Week 1–2: engineering spike + integration validate int8 quantization on internal eval set; enable KV cache prototype; bench unified 13b-int8 throughput on dedicated instance types. Owners: Arjun (quant), Noah (bench).
- Week 3: rollout canary at 5% traffic with full instrumentation; AB quality checks (embedding delta thresholds). Owner: Maya.
- Week 4: expand to 30% if metrics pass; enable batching policy with conservative latency SLO (p95 < 1.2x baseline).
- Week 5–6: full rollout, shift background jobs to spot pools; reduce log retention to 14d (optional).

Rollback criteria (predefined):
- Quality regression: embedding drift beyond 0.08 average cos distance on the held eval; increase in user-reported NPS drop > 1.2 points (in 7-day rolling).
- Latency regression: p95 generation latency > 1.6x baseline for more than 3 consecutive hours.
- Error rate: 5xxs increase > 0.5% absolute.

Open questions / risks:
- Quantization compatibility across model ops: we observed two ops with numerical instability on proprietary plugins; may need small kernel patch or fallback to mixed-precision for those ops. Jira ticket linked (JIRA:OPT-7890).
- Customer product constraints: Stellar’s enterprise customers require 99.9% uptime and audit trails; moving some background traffic to spot needs legal sign-off (CSR review).
- Monitoring: need to add per-route quality regression alerts tied to known prompt set; recommend shipping Redwood Optimize’s eval-monitoring rule pack.

Recommendations & next steps:
- Accept base projection and schedule the 6-week implementation with a 5% canary starting week-of-11/04.
- Add a short-term checkpoint to re-run sensitivity with real canary hit rate after 72 hours; update savings estimate.
- Work with Stellar billing to create a dedicated reserved pool for background workload to isolate cost and enable spot savings.

Appendix (quick tables exported from modeling sheet):
- Traffic mix: Short(1–32 tokens): 70% (2.24M req/day), Long(33–1024): 30% (0.96M req/day)
- Cache assumptions: 27% global hit (prefix heavy), estimated 0.44M req/day hit -> saves avg 420 tokens/request on hit subset.
- Batching latency impact: expected p50 delta +8ms, p95 delta +48ms (within SLO).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working sheet; numbers are modeled from a snapshot of Stellar's usage (billing export 2024-09) and internal Redwood perf profiles. Please flag any customer-specific contractual constraints before we schedule the canary.
- If approved, I'll convert the model into a shared Google Sheet with live parameters: cache-hit %, batch-size, quantization gain % so CS and Solutions Eng can run scenario analysis.

Contact / owner: Maya Chen (product-optimize) — maya@redwoodai.example
